brief: NDX has broken below range lows and the longer-term trend line, trading well below the 200-day moving average and down more than 5% intraday, while tech volatility approaches Liberation Day panic levels both outright and relative to VIX, which is itself surging. The crowded AI trade continues to unwind, with relative winners emerging outside the AI complex. GS data: non-dealer futures selling of $5.1bn between October 20 and 27 ended three weeks of buying, but net length stayed at the 96th percentile on a two-year lookback, so the crowded long trade had barely unwound. Nasdaq then fell 5.6% from October 27 to November 2 as futures open interest surged $16.3bn, including a $14.3bn jump on October 30, the largest daily increase of 2026 outside roll periods, which GS reads as aggressive new short selling. Nasdaq rebounded 1.6% from November 2 to 4 while open interest fell $4.1bn and funding recovered versus SPX, which the note attributes to short covering rather than a return of bullish conviction. Separately, the note's long-Apple-versus-NVDA anti-AI trade continues to outperform, arguing for selectivity within tech rather than abandoning it.
